## Create

### SCSS

- For SCSS variable output, every SCSS variable should reference a CSS variable. This is so that the system can be themed by just changing CSS variables without needing to modify SCSS variables.
  - The only exception to this are SCSS color variables. This is because consumers of SCSS color variables are using SCSS transform values on them like lighten(), opacify(), etc, which do not work against a CSS variable.

## Build

- In order to build, use the `build` script in the package.json:
  `npm run build`

## Custom Configuration

#### Auto generating HSL Tokens

1. We want an HSL variant of each base color token however we don't want to have to define it, or calculate the HSL.

- In order to achieve this, there are several parts that were implemented.
  - New transform groups called `mds/css` and `mds/scss`. These apply the `attribute/color` transform to add additional attributes to any token with `category: "base-color"` such as HSL, RGB, HEX. They also apply a custom transform `mds/color/hsl`.
  - New transform `mds/color/hsl` which adds a new attribute `hslArgumentString` to any token with `category: "base-color"`. The `hslArgumentString` is the internal bits of the HSL function, e.g. `240, 60%, 55%`.
  - New formats called `mds/css/variables` and `mds/scss/variables` which perform the default output from SD + a new function which will automatically add the HSL color variables to any token with `category: "base-color"`, using the `hslArgumentString` as the value of the HSL variable.

2. We want to be able to indicate certain tokens being platform specific. Simply add a property `platforms` with an array of platform names as strings. Any token without this property will build for all platforms. This is done via the custom formatter for CSS & SCSS.

3. Some values have different outputs for different platforms and they're so different that transforms would not work to create the platform specific variations. In this case, a new property was added called `valueOverrides` which is an object with properties for each platform specific value. If a platform specific value is not included as a property, the `value` property will be used. This is done via the custom formatter for CSS & SCSS.
